job_taken.what: OBSERVE 1/3 - the job execution is now IN_PROGRESS. The device is holding here before it generates a key pair.
job_taken.console:
Console: AWS IoT console -> Manage -> Remote actions -> Jobs -> your job -> Job executions
           {}

overlap.what: OBSERVE 2/3 - the overlap window. The new certificate is signed, ACTIVE and attached, and the current one is still attached and working. The thing has TWO certificates right now, which is exactly why a failed rotation cannot lock the device out.
overlap.console:
Console: AWS IoT console -> Manage -> Things -> your thing -> Certificates
           {}
overlap.expect: Expect:  two principals listed. The new one ends in {}.

retired.what: OBSERVE 3/3 - the cutover succeeded, so the old certificate is being set INACTIVE. The retirement is event-driven, so give it a moment and re-run the command if it still shows ACTIVE. It is not deleted yet: retirement is deferred so a device that reappears late can still be recovered.
retired.console:
Console: AWS IoT console -> Security -> Certificates (the old one now shows Inactive)
           {}
retired.cli:
CLI:     Use the OTHER certificate id you saw at OBSERVE 2 - the one that is not the new certificate:
             aws iot describe-certificate --certificate-id <thatId> \
               --query "certificateDescription.status"   (expect: INACTIVE)
retired.scheduler:
CLI:     aws scheduler list-schedules --name-prefix ws-aws-iot-dm-adv-prov-revoke- \
               --query "Schedules[].[Name,State]"
             The one-time deletion timer. Its name ends with the first 16 characters of the retired certificate id.
